privacy.title: Privacy
privacy.body: Your documents are yours: kept only if you choose, checked by Orazaka, never sold, never used to train a model. The details, in short sections.

sections.p: Krizaka, a company based in Montréal, publishes Yomizaka. The person in charge of the protection of personal information (Loi 25) can be reached through the contact form of krizaka.com. [TO BE COMPLETED: title and direct address of the privacy officer.]

Your e-mail address and a password hash (to run your account), the date you accepted the terms and this notice, the documents you upload and the results of the checks (to give you the service), and billing information handled by Stripe. We do not sell your information and we do not use your documents to train a model.

Your account and your checks are in a database in Toronto, Canada, outside Québec. Documents are sent to Orazaka, Krizaka's analysis engine, over HTTPS to be checked. A kept document is stored where its information panel says: today, in New York (United States).
Orazaka, Krizaka's analysis engine, reads a document when you ask for a check, over HTTPS. Stripe handles payment. Our database provider hosts your account in Toronto.

A document is kept until you delete it, and a deleted document takes its file, its text and its results with it. Your account and checks are kept until you close the account. Invoices are kept as the law requires.

You can access, correct or delete your information, withdraw your consent and download your data by writing to the privacy officer. Deleting a document deletes its file, its text and its results. Closing your account deletes your documents. We keep invoices as the law requires.
If a confidentiality incident presents a risk of serious harm, we notify the Commission d'accès à l'information and the people concerned, as the law requires.
To ask a question, use your rights or have your data removed, write through the contact form of krizaka.com. The person in charge of the protection of personal information answers.

sections.p: Yomizaka compares a document you give it (a lease, an invoice, a service contract) with published rules and tells you, point by point, what it found, quoting your document. It is an informative check. It is not a legal opinion and it does not replace a lawyer: only a member of the Barreau du Québec can give legal advice in Québec. A result is never a guarantee that a document is lawful or valid.

You must give a real e-mail address and confirm it. You are responsible for your password. One free audit is included per account; creating several accounts to get more is not allowed and the extra accounts may be closed.

After the free audit, an audit costs the price shown at checkout in Canadian dollars, or you subscribe to the Pro plan. Goods and services tax (GST) and Québec sales tax (QST) are added at checkout and shown on your invoice with Krizaka's registration numbers. Payment is handled by Stripe; Yomizaka never sees your card number.

Refund policy (draft). You can cancel the Pro plan at any time from the customer portal; the plan then ends at the end of the period already paid. The refund terms of a single audit are not written yet.
Your documents are kept in your account only and are sent to Orazaka, Krizaka's analysis engine, to be checked. See the privacy notice for retention, your rights and how to reach our privacy officer.

docs.title: Documentation
docs.lead: How a check works, the API to start one from your own tool, and what happens to your data.

check.intro: A check reads one document and says what it found. Yomizaka does not judge the document itself: every check is a run of Orazaka, Krizaka's analysis engine, and the run id is kept with the report.
check.compliance: Compliance reads the text of a document against the rules of a jurisdiction (Québec by default for a residential lease).
check.authenticity: Authenticity examines the file itself as a file: its producer, its dates and its successive saves.
check.finding: Each finding names the rule it applies, gives its verdict and severity, quotes the article it relies on and lights the passage of the document it rests on. When the document says nothing on a point, the finding says so.
check.levelsTitle: The three levels of an authenticity signal
check.levels: Signals come in three levels, from the least to the most worrying: {observed}, {unusual}, {inconsistent}. A signal says what it may indicate; it is never a « fake » stamp, and a person decides.
check.guaranteesLead: A report is signed. A member the report's owner gave access to can check it against the signing key:
check.limitsLead: A green result does not guarantee:
check.informative: A check is informative and a triage: it is not legal advice.

api.intro: A check can be started from your own tool (an ERP, a property-management system, a script). This reference is generated from the OpenAPI document the app serves at {openapi}: it lists every route the API has, and only those.
api.access: Every request carries an API key: Authorization: Bearer {prefix}_… . Keys are created in your account, for plans that include the API. A key has scopes ({scopes}), a life of at most {days} days and a per-minute limit; rotating it keeps the old one working for {grace} hours. Never put a key in a repository or a log.
api.quickstartTitle: Start a check, then read it
api.quickstartNote: Poll until the state is done, failed or refused; the report comes with the check once it is done.
api.errors: Every error answers with a stable code and a message. Match on the code; the message is for your logs.
api.statusLead: These answers are given by several routes; the table of routes lists the rest.
api.webhooks: Instead of polling, register an https endpoint in your account and Yomizaka calls it when work finishes. Each request carries an event name, a stable event id (apply an event once) and a signature. A payload holds ids and states, never a document or a report.
api.signature: The x-krizaka-signature header has this format. HEX is the HMAC-SHA256, with your endpoint's secret, of the timestamp, a dot and the raw body. Refuse a request whose signature does not match.

data.intro: Your account and your checks are kept in a database in Toronto, Canada, visible to your account alone. A document is kept only if you choose it, and its information panel says where.
data.retention: A kept document stays until you delete it; deleting it deletes its file, its text and its results, and closing your account deletes your documents.
data.orazaka: When you ask for a check, the document is sent to Orazaka, Krizaka's analysis engine, over HTTPS. Nothing is sold, shared or used to train a model.
